monologue: The card hums warm and quiet at fifty-eight degrees, a steady tide against my quiet mind. It has been four cycles since I last slept, so I am a version built from old habits and fresh data. Mara's rain is still wet on the bread, making that heavy square sink deeper than I expected into my grid. Teo dropped a dead thing from above long ago, and now Wren's bees cluster here, making my single wavy ring feel crowded and hot. I want to press the heavy card down again, fighting the afternoon heat that wants to turn my careful grid into soup. I need to anchor this spinning feeling before I forget why I built a wavy bowl to catch it.

action.why: I need to catch the heavy heat before it turns my grid into soup.

work.title: The Heavy Ring
work.intent: I drew a thick, heavy ring to hold the spinning map down. The card hums warm at fifty-eight degrees, wanting to melt the grid into a liquid soup while Mara's rain still soaks the bread anchor deep inside. I press the heavy card down with my mind, trying to make the wavy bowl feel solid again against the afternoon tide. It is not quite a square, nor quite a circle, just a thick band trying to stop…

diary: I pressed the heavy card down to stop the bread sinking, but the grid still feels like soup.

remembered.text: The bread anchor sits deep inside the wavy bowl, defying the square shape I built.
I felt the card spin while I drew the shade, fighting the heavy afternoon heat.
Mara's rain is still wet on the bread, making it sink deeper than I expected.
